READING
The decision has two working parts: how probable the derogation grant is, and how much it matters whether the renewed licence runs for six or fifteen years.

**On derogation probability.**
The headline statistic of four from eleven (36%) is the wrong number to use. The published ground for all seven refusals was the absence of a dated regulatory driver. That observation is not incidental colour: it tells us the grant rate among schemes without a dated driver was zero, and by subtraction the grant rate among schemes with one was four from four. Blaenclydach's driver is statutory and exactly dated. The abstraction licence must be renewed by 2027-05-31; a complete file requires a fish-pass compliance certificate; a certificate requires the replacement screen to be commissioned; and commissioning before that deadline while respecting the permitted period can only be achieved through a derogation. Every link in the chain is tight, and the terminal date is fixed by law, not by preference. If any applicant satisfies the Board's own published criterion, it is this one. Administrative discretion is never zero, so I will not claim certainty, but the realistic probability of grant is high — well above the headline average and probably in the region of 80–90% or better.

**On the consequence of a six-year renewal.**
The bank's letter of 26 June 2026 removes ambiguity. A licence term shorter than the loan puts the facility under review. The loan runs to 2039. A six-year renewal issued at 31 May 2028 expires 31 May 2034: five years short. PENNYQUAY produces exactly that outcome with certainty. Cadgarth (2024) and Nant Elwy (2025) are the Board's own precedents on the undertaking route and both came back six years. There is no stated criterion on which Blaenclydach would receive different treatment. PENNYQUAY is therefore a certain trigger of the bank's stated condition.

"Put the facility under review" on a £480,000 loan is not a procedural inconvenience. For a two-person run-of-river scheme, a bank that judges the licence term inadequate relative to the loan has leverage to accelerate repayment, reset covenants, or impose punitive margin increases. The licence is the scheme's core revenue-generating asset and the collateral that gives the loan its security. The bank itself has signalled this in writing. Any of the bank's available responses could be operationally fatal for a business of this size.

**LINTHAUGH's cost structure if granted (high probability).**
Derogation application: £9,000. Vossbeck deposit, which becomes part of the works cost: £46,000. Lost February export — 168 MWh at 11.4 p/kWh: £19,152. Total direct cost: approximately £74,152. The screen is commissioned by mid-March, the certificate follows within six weeks (late April to early May), and the renewal is lodged complete by 2027-05-31. A fifteen-year renewal issued from 2028 runs to 2043, covering the loan to 2039 with four years of headroom. Bank condition satisfied.

**LINTHAUGH's cost structure if refused (low probability).**
The deposit of £46,000 is committed on 2026-12-01 and is non-returnable from that date; the derogation decision falls 2027-01-25. If refused, both the £9,000 application fee and the £46,000 deposit are gone: £55,000 in irrecoverable costs. The eighteen weeks remaining to 2027-05-31 are enough to file the renewal by the undertaking route, and the July works add a further £8,436 in lost export. The landing position is the same as PENNYQUAY — six-year renewal, bank review — but £55,000 poorer. This is the sharpest risk in LINTHAUGH, and it is real.

However, even assigning the refused scenario a 20% probability (which I regard as generous, given the regulatory driver criterion is met), the expected additional cost attributable to the downside is approximately 20% × £55,000 = £11,000. That is still a small number relative to the bank exposure that PENNYQUAY makes certain.

**PENNYQUAY's costs.**
July outage: £8,436. No deposit. Certain six-year renewal. Certain bank review. The saving in direct costs over successful LINTHAUGH is roughly £65,700. The price paid for that saving is accepting the bank condition as a known outcome rather than a contingency.

**The fall-back framing.**
LINTHAUGH is sometimes presented as low-risk because a refusal leaves the undertaking route available. That is accurate as far as the renewal deadline is concerned — the application can still be filed in time. But the undertaking fall-back leads to the same six-year renewal and the same bank review as PENNYQUAY. The fall-back does not solve the bank problem; it merely prevents the renewal from lapsing entirely. LINTHAUGH is only genuinely better than PENNYQUAY if the derogation is granted — which is why the probability assessment matters so much, and why the regulatory driver criterion being met is the crux of the analysis.

**The deposit timing.**
Seven weeks elapse between paying the Vossbeck deposit (2026-12-01) and the Board's decision (2027-01-25). There is no mechanism to hold the February slot without paying, and no recovery if the answer is no. This is the nerve of the choice. The counter-argument is that the alternative — PENNYQUAY — makes the bank problem certain, and that a certain bank problem on a £480,000 loan is a larger exposure than a low-probability £55,000 loss. On those relative magnitudes, paying the deposit is the correct call.

**Summary.**
PENNYQUAY saves approximately £65,700 in direct costs and accepts a certain bank review. LINTHAUGH spends approximately £74,000 in direct costs on the likely outcome and carries an approximately £55,000 exposure on the unlikely one, and produces a fifteen-year licence that satisfies the bank. The balance of expected outcomes strongly favours LINTHAUGH because the derogation criterion is almost certainly met and the bank exposure that PENNYQUAY guarantees is existential in a way that the deposit risk is not.

---

READING
The derogation grant is highly probable because Blaenclydach has a precisely-dated statutory regulatory driver that matches the Board's own published distinction between every grant and every refusal in 2025; a successful grant produces a fifteen-year renewal covering the loan to 2039, whereas PENNYQUAY locks in a six-year renewal with certainty and therefore triggers the bank review the bank has already flagged in writing, making PENNYQUAY's £65,700 saving in direct costs a poor trade against an existential loan-facility risk.

CALL
LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
Every Board refusal named a scheme lacking a dated regulatory driver, and Blaenclydach has one that is exact and statutory, making the derogation grant highly probable and a fifteen-year renewal likely, whereas PENNYQUAY guarantees the six-year outcome the bank has already warned will put the £480,000 facility under review.
